sections.overview: A widespread northern-hemisphere fly, it is often associated with large-mammal dung.
sections.identification: Males are yellow-orange and hairy; females are greener and less hairy.
sections.habitat: Adults gather at fresh dung, often in temperate pastures.
sections.diet: Larvae feed in dung. Adults prey on small insects and may also take nectar.
sections.behavior: Males wait on or near fresh dung for females.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in dung. The species overwinters as a pupa.
sections.ecology: Its larvae help break down mammal dung.
sections.conservation: The natural-history review gives no global conservation assessment.
